narrative.summary: A real, heavily-used cross-chain messaging layer - 709 OApps already registered - owned by a bespoke 5-of-7 multisig that isn’t a Gnosis Safe at all.
narrative.detail: A live eth_getLogs replay of DelegateSet on LayerZero’s own EndpointV2, from genesis to the chain tip, found 965 events from 709 distinct OApp addresses already registered - a real, active messaging surface an order of magnitude larger than everything this oracle tracked before, and structurally separate from the chain’s own L1 rollup bridge above. EndpointV2, SendUln302 and ReceiveUln302 were each checked independently and all three share the identical owner() - deliberately NOT a Gnosis Safe (getOwners()/getThreshold() both revert on it), but a bespoke on-chain multisig confirmed live as a real 5-of-7 via its own getSigners()/threshold() interface. Executor, a fourth LayerZero contract, was deliberately excluded: its own admin resolves to a third, still-unidentified contract matching neither pattern - an open thread, not guessed at. Only this shared infrastructure is scored - the 709 individual OApps built on top of it are not tracked one by one.
